owner: constraint-layered coordinate assignment and orthogonal routing
problem: Fixed-coordinate route checks can accept a drawing that is dominated after a legal coordinate reassignment.
scope: All nodes, ports, ranks, component libraries and acyclic left-to-right input graphs; no kind, name, size-tier or fixture-specific branch. Rendering-only replicas are permitted only for zero-indegree nodes.
baseline: The asymmetric merge fixture passes the old oracle with 8 bends although a legal 6-bend drawing exists.
benchmarks: ELK layered Brandes-Koepf placement with edge straightening
OGDF orthogonal layout with bend bounds and compaction
yFiles hierarchical layout with exact ports, grouping and incremental optimization
advantages: Existing layout already has exact port geometry and independent global quality metrics
Layer order and rank constraints bound the one-dimensional coordinate search
disadvantages: Current placement and routing are optimized in separate phases
Current route dominance oracle freezes node coordinates
limitations: Global bend and crossing minimization is combinatorial
Commercial yFiles cannot be a bundled runtime dependency
defects: A four-bend edge can pass when a legal node-coordinate change yields two bends
A narrow terminal-only move would overfit one visible symptom
A single visual anchor for a widely dispersed zero-indegree source can force a long crossing-heavy distribution line

metrics.name: known_good_acceptance

metrics.measurement: Enumerate legal rank-order-preserving coordinate and orthogonal-route candidates independently

metrics.name: hard_quality_regressions

metrics.name: stress_4096_runtime
metrics.measurement: Generate and inspect the frozen 4096-clock scenario

hypotheses: A rank-order-preserving coordinate channel graph can expose dominated drawings without component-specific rules
Conflict-window exact search plus global dominance validation can reduce bends without worsening hard metrics
Spatial indexing and suspect-window filtering keep work near linear on repeated large structures
allowed_variables: node y coordinates within rank-order constraints
rendering-only anchor count and continuous consumer partition for zero-indegree nodes

stages.input: frozen good and bad layout documents
stages.checker: pytest with positive, negative and injected-fault assertions
stages.rollback: revert oracle change if any good baseline is rejected
allowed_variables: quality oracle implementation and test fixtures

stages.input: ranked nodes, exact ports and routed edges
stages.output: globally accepted coordinate and route updates
stages.checker: independent quality oracle plus metric dominance
full tests, random corpus, stress tests and extracted-package smoke
stages.rollback: revert to the last fully passing commit

hard_gates: no additional different-net overlap or crossing
no fixture, node-name, component-kind or size-tier branch
every logical edge is drawn exactly once
only zero-indegree logical nodes may have rendering replicas
failure_fixtures: mirrored asymmetric merge long branch a
mutated library geometry and port anchors
fault_injections: restore a dominated four-bend route and old node coordinate
offer a bend-reducing move that collides with a node label
offer a bend-reducing move that adds a different-net crossing
replace component kinds while preserving geometry and graph structure
replicate a non-root node or drop one edge while splitting a root
rollback: Keep the previous document and production commit whenever any hard metric regresses.

iteration_budget.review_trigger: one good-baseline rejection or two failures of the same search representation

stop_conditions: zero independently avoidable joint bends in the declared corpus
all hard quality metrics remain passing
frozen and downloaded release packages pass

promotion_decision.reason: The method is reusable across left-to-right port-constrained layered diagrams.

writeback: Project-specific evidence stays in the goal; generic joint optimization and oracle rules update the user-root clock-tree-layout skill.
